t: Nothing in this Act, or any amendments made by this Act, shall be construed so as to affect the authority vested in the Commissioner of the District of Columbia or the authority vested in the District of Columbia Council by Reorganization Plan Numbered 3 of 1967. The performance of any function vested by this Act in the Commissioner of the District of Columbia or in any office or agency under his jurisdiction and control, or in the District of Columbia Council, may be delegated by the Commissioner or by the Council, as the case may be, in accordance with the provisions of such plan.

fable.w: This is a savings clause that preserves the authority of the District of Columbia Commissioner and Council under Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1967 and permits them to delegate their functions. The tempting reading is that a reference to the D.C. Council, a local-type body, signals coordination with an outside party. That fails because the section sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue before a federal decision; it only addresses internal allocation and delegation of authority.
fable.s: may be delegated by the Commissioner or by the Council, as the case may be, in accordance with the provisions of such plan

opus.w: This section only keeps the existing authority of the D.C. Commissioner and Council in place and lets them delegate functions under the 1967 Reorganization Plan. It sets up no process for any outside party to be consulted on, comment on, or challenge a federal decision. It may look relevant because the D.C. Council is a local government body, but here the Council is simply exercising and delegating its own powers, not taking part in a federal agency's decision.
opus.s: The performance of any function vested by this Act in the Commissioner of the District of Columbia or in any office or agency under his jurisdiction and control, or in the District of Columbia Council, may be delegated by the Commissioner or by the Council, as the case may be, in accordance with the provisions of such plan.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that the District of Columbia Council is a local, non-federal body, so mentioning it might bring an outside party into a federal decision. That fails the DEFINITION. The section is a savings clause that preserves the Commissioner's and the Council's existing authority. It also lets each of them delegate their own functions under Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1967. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted or coordinated with before a federal decision. There is no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking requirement, or right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the internal delegation of authority within the District of Columbia government (Commissioner and Council). It does not describe the federal government consulting with an outside party before making a decision. The definition requires the federal government to consult with outside entities; here, the text is about local government internal procedures.
qwen_chat.s: The performance of any function vested by this Act in the Commissioner of the District of Columbia or in any office or agency under his jurisdiction and control, or in the District of Columbia Council, may be delegated by the Commissioner or by the Council, as the case may be, in accordance with the provisions of such plan.
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the District of Columbia Council or the Commissioner are "outside" the federal government because D.C. has a unique local government structure. However, under the definition provided, local governments and their officials are generally considered outside entities *only* if they are distinct from the federal government in the context of the decision-making process described. Here, the text is purely about internal delegation of authority within the D.C. government structure as defined by a Reorganization Plan. It does not describe a process where the federal government (e.g., the President, Congress, or a federal agency) consults with an outside party before making a decision. It simply clarifies that existing authorities remain intact and can be delegated internally. There is no consultation, comment period, advisory board with outside members, or right to sue mentioned. The actors involved (Commissioner, Council, agencies under their jurisdiction) are part of the local government structure, but the text does not describe a federal decision-making process involving outside participation. It is a savings clause regarding internal administrative authority.

Actually, looking closer at the definition: "States, tribes, local governments... are OUTSIDE it." The District of Columbia Council is a local government body. However, the text does not describe the *federal government* consulting with them. It describes the *Commissioner* or *Council* delegating functions *within* their own jurisdiction. The definition requires "the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." This section does not describe the federal government making a decision based on consultation with the D.C. Council. It describes the D.C. Council's internal powers. Therefore, there is no participation as defined.
